question:
If $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&-3\\3&2&1\\1&2&-1\end{bmatrix}$, find $A^{-1}$ and hence solve the following system of equations:
$$2x+y-3z=13$$
$$3x+2y+z=4$$
$$x+2y-z=8$$
explanation:
Step 1 Find the determinant of $A$:
$$|A|=2\begin{vmatrix}2&1\\2&-1\end{vmatrix}-1\begin{vmatrix}3&1\\1&-1\end{vmatrix}-3\begin{vmatrix}3&2\\1&2\end{vmatrix}$$
$$=2(-4)-(-4)-12=-16.$$
Since $|A|\neq0$, the matrix is invertible.

Step 2 Compute the cofactors:
$$C_{11}=-4,\;C_{12}=4,\;C_{13}=4,$$
$$C_{21}=-5,\;C_{22}=1,\;C_{23}=-3,$$
$$C_{31}=7,\;C_{32}=-11,\;C_{33}=1.$$
Hence,
$$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-4&-5&7\\4&1&-11\\4&-3&1\end{bmatrix}.$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A$$
$$=\frac{1}{16}\begin{bmatrix}4&5&-7\\-4&-1&11\\-4&3&-1\end{bmatrix}.$$

Step 3 Write the system in matrix form $AX=B$, where
$$X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix},\qquad B=\begin{bmatrix}13\\4\\8\end{bmatrix}.$$
Then
$$X=A^{-1}B.$$

Step 4 Multiply:
$$X=\frac{1}{16}\begin{bmatrix}4&5&-7\\-4&-1&11\\-4&3&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}13\\4\\8\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\frac{1}{16}\begin{bmatrix}52+20-56\\-52-4+88\\-52+12-8\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\frac{1}{16}\begin{bmatrix}16\\32\\-48\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\-3\end{bmatrix}.$$

Step 5 Therefore, the solution of the system is:
$$\boxed{x=1,\quad y=2,\quad z=-3.}$$
